headline: Rain moving up the coast arrives Sunday afternoon and lasts into early Monday, with less than an inch in New York City and 1–2 inches farther east, but the bigger story is a likely strong coastal storm Wednesday night through Friday bringing heavy rain, strong east winds and widespread coastal flooding over Thanksgiving.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Dense fog has formed early Sunday across Long Island and southern Queens, with visibility a quarter mile or less in many spots, and a Dense Fog Advisory runs until 9 AM; it is unclear whether the fog will spread inland, so the advisory could be expanded. Low pressure moving up the coast brings light rain as early as late Sunday morning or early afternoon, becoming moderate to heavy at times from mid-afternoon into the evening, mainly east of the city. Rain totals have trended down: less than an inch for New York City and the western half of the area (only a few tenths in the far western suburbs), versus 1–2 inches for the eastern half, with the heaviest on eastern Long Island and southeastern Connecticut Sunday evening and overnight. Winds turn east then northeast at 10–15 mph with coastal gusts to 25–30 mph, and a very low chance of brief 40–45 mph gusts right along the coast of eastern Long Island and southeastern Connecticut; Sunday is mild, with forecast highs near 63 at Islip and 61 at Bridgeport, just shy of records (64).

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: The storm pulls away quickly to the northeast, and any lingering showers end by daybreak Monday as winds shift to the northwest. Monday is dry with west-northwest gusts around 15–20 mph, and Tuesday and most of Wednesday stay dry as a large, strong high-pressure system settles over the Northeast. East-northeast winds start to pick up Wednesday evening, with rain possible late Wednesday night.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Computer models continue to agree on a potentially large, high-impact coastal storm from Wednesday night into Thanksgiving Day and Friday, likely worse for wind and coastal flooding than Sunday's system. The strong high to the north squeezed against the storm approaching from the south could produce east-northeast wind gusts of 35–45 mph sometime Thursday or Thursday night. A period of moderate to heavy rain is likely on Thanksgiving, though the storm's fast movement should limit flooding from rain; small changes in the complex pattern could still shift its strength, track and timing considerably.

coast: Sunday night's storm poses only a minimal coastal flood threat at worst: the south-shore back bays of Nassau County might just touch minor flood levels at the Monday morning high tide, a statement may be needed, and water could fall short if the storm keeps trending east. The bigger concern is Wednesday night through Friday: tides run high with Tuesday's full moon, many locations need less than a foot of extra water to reach minor flooding, and the current forecast supports widespread minor to moderate coastal flooding, possibly localized major flooding, plus beach flooding, erosion and overwash. On the water, Small Craft Advisories run Sunday evening to 6 AM Monday for New York Harbor, Long Island Sound and the bays, and from 3 PM Sunday to 6 PM Monday for the near-shore ocean waters, with a Gale Warning from 6 PM Sunday to 6 AM Monday for the outer ocean waters (the earlier Gale Watch for near-shore waters was dropped). Rough ocean seas linger into Monday night, with only a brief lull Tuesday afternoon and night before east-northeast winds build Wednesday to gale force Wednesday night and storm force on the ocean Thursday; waves could reach 12–20 feet on the ocean (20–25 feet out east), 7–10 feet on Block Island Sound and 4–6 feet on Long Island Sound and at the entrance to New York Harbor.
watch_for: Wednesday night–Friday coastal storm: heavy rain Thanksgiving, gusts 35–45 mph, and widespread minor to moderate (possibly localized major) coastal flooding; track and timing could still change.
Sunday afternoon–night rain: the storm's track decides how far west the heavier rain reaches; NYC is currently on the lighter side (under an inch).
Early Sunday dense fog on Long Island and southern Queens could spread inland before improving.
confidence: Confidence is low on whether the Sunday morning fog spreads inland and moderate for Sunday's rain and wind, which depend on the storm's exact track; models agree a significant coastal storm is likely Wednesday night through Friday, but its strength, track and timing remain uncertain.
